liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Believe It or Not** (3 reviews): Reviewer says Jerry hits every lyric and Bobby never squeals or howls, with all notes placed correctly; Believe It or Not later stands out, since it never entered regular rotation [13][18][19]
- **Minglewood Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls Minglewood choppy but danceable; Around 7:45 into Minglewood, about 20 seconds of Jerry and Brent tuning appears, leading toward Brown Eyed Women [17][22]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Sugaree runs under eight minutes, which the reviewer finds disappointingly short, with typical Jerry trills [17]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer recalls a spacey intro to China Cat Sunflower [16]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Jam just before I Know You Rider includes a section resembling their older transition jam [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Believe It or Not**: rare: 9 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd88-09-09.sbd.unknown.14840.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 138 min; rated 3.44/5 by 16 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard sound unusually deep and not flat, which they usually find in soundboards; Streamed copy on iTunes has uneven tracking, with breaks between songs arriving about three seconds into the next track; Reviewer feels the tape fails to capture the live atmosphere well [12][13][15][16][20]
- **gd1988-09-09.148147.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 144 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1988-09-09.145671.ots.akg460.ackerman.miller.noel.t-flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 135 min [7]
- **gd1988-09-09.110654.senn441.boeditaper.flac6**: source not stated; 22 songs; 137 min [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended as their first show and had only owned a first-set tape for years [12]
- Reviewer returned to shows after a three-year absence, having been put off by the mid-80s scene [14]
- Crowd energy was the most intense the reviewer ever felt, and the band responded to it [15]
- Reviewer recalls lighting crew members up in the rafters, which they found trippy [15]
- Reviewer says Brent plays prominently throughout and Jerry drives the night [16]
- Attendee recalls the crowd thinking the band was starting Gomorrah because the opening chords sounded similar [18]
- Fans camped in the park across from the Spectrum, following the earlier Landover shows [20]
- Reviewer sees the show as typical of 1988, a standout year for the band [13]
- Setlist looks standard on paper, but the reviewer found the actual show far more powerful than it appears [14]
- Reviewer finds the sound better than the night before, though still not explosive [17]
- Reviewer thinks this show is slightly better than the night before, despite a less interesting song list [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd88-09-09.sbd.unknown.14840.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > Cass Master > DAT > CDR > CDR > EAC > SHN [1]. Also: Soundboard to cassette master, then DAT, two CDR generations, EAC extraction and SHN [1]
- **gd1988-09-09.148147.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [3]. Also: Patch source for the I Will Take You Home to Quinn transition came from Don Crandall, Chris Huron and Ted Mattes [3]
- **gd1988-09-09.145671.ots.akg460.ackerman.miller.noel.t-flac16**: taped by Ray Ackerman; transferred by Joe Noel and Charlie Miller; source: Ray Ackerman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG 460 w/ck63 caps > AKG B18 phantom power unit > Sony D5 [7]. Also: Edited and mastered by Joe Noel from masters shared by Ray, with an unknown taper's patch [7]
- **gd1988-09-09.110654.senn441.boeditaper.flac6**: taped by Boeditaper; transferred by boeditaper; source: Sony D6 Cassette Master>Sennheiser 441 Mics>Sony TC- We 325 Home Cassette Deck(Playback)>Harmon Kardon CDR 20 Home Burner>CDR>EAC>Flac. [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Kirsten Michel: [1988-09-09 The Spectrum, Philadelphia, PA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1988-09-09-the-spectrum-philadelphia-pa-usa/) [24]
